title: DynamoDB Data Modeling & Performance
summary: Keys, indexes, capacity modes, DAX, Streams and global tables for single-digit-millisecond access.
tldr: Design keys from **access patterns**: a high-cardinality **partition key** spreads load; a **sort key** lets one `Query` fetch a range (for example vehicle ID + timestamp).
A new query on a non-key attribute → **global secondary index**, then `Query` it. A `Scan` with a filter still reads (and bills) the whole table.
One hot key throttling while the table is under capacity → **write sharding** (random suffix). Microsecond reads with the same API → **DAX**. Multi-Region active-active → **global tables**.

keyFacts.text: One **RCU** = one strongly consistent read/s of up to 4 KB (or two eventually consistent). One **WCU** = one write/s of up to 1 KB. Round item size up.
Per-partition ceiling of RCU and WCU. **Adaptive capacity** shifts throughput to busy partitions but can't lift one key past this limit.
**Burst capacity** keeps up to five minutes of unused throughput to absorb short spikes. Auto scaling reacts in minutes, too slow for 30-second bursts.
Maximum item size. Store big objects in S3 and keep a pointer in the item.
**DynamoDB Streams** retention. Streams feed Lambda and EventBridge Pipes, and they carry replication for eventually consistent global tables.
**Global tables** default to multi-Region eventual consistency (last writer wins). Multi-Region strong consistency must be chosen at creation and can't be switched later.

keywords.cue: all readings for one vehicle in a time range
keywords.answer: Partition key vehicle ID, sort key timestamp, Query with BETWEEN

keywords.cue: Scan with filter is slow and costly for a new lookup
keywords.answer: GSI on that attribute, then Query

keywords.cue: one key throttled while table capacity mostly unused
keywords.answer: Hot partition: write sharding with a random suffix

keywords.cue: microsecond reads, same DynamoDB API, no cache invalidation code
absorb 20–30 second spikes over provisioned capacity
skewed traffic but total under provisioned capacity
multi-Region writes, survive a Region failure, no promotion
react to item changes, filter without Lambda
600 strongly consistent reads/s of 6 KB items

traps: DAX speeds up **reads**; it doesn't fix a hot partition for writes or add write capacity.
Raising table capacity or switching to on-demand doesn't fix one hot key, because the per-partition limit still applies.
An LSI can't be added to an existing table and shares the base table's partition key, so it can't serve a lookup by a different attribute.
A GSI on the same hot attribute just moves the hot partition into the index.
DAX serves eventually consistent reads; strongly consistent reads pass through to the table.
ElastiCache in front of DynamoDB needs cache-aside code and invalidation logic; when the question says "same DynamoDB API, no invalidation code", pick **DAX**.
Aurora Global Database has a single writer Region and needs a failover step, so "write locally in every Region with no promotion" points to **DynamoDB global tables**.
